body:
**RAV-RUN3-R1-F003 [low] CLI help** — CLI help omits the `--registry-live` network exception

`--input-json` says it is offline, but `--registry-live` remains an explicit network exception. The help text can name that exception.

**RAV-RUN3-R1-F004 [low] registry reporting** — The CLI prints an initial zero-count registry status before live lookups

The CLI prints registry status before live lookups. A final status line would show the actual query and error totals.

One final status line before publication checks can replace the initial zero-count line.

**RAV-RUN3-R1-F005 [low] CLI** — `--limit 0` processes all models

`--limit 0` processes all models. Negative limits use Python negative slicing.

Negative limits can be rejected, and slicing can run whenever the value is not `None`.

**RAV-RUN1-R1-F002 [low] CLI help** — The top-level `every_eval_ever validate` help says directory arguments are unsupported

The top-level `every_eval_ever validate` help still says directory arguments are unsupported. The existing help text can describe recursive directory expansion.

**RAV-RUN1-R1-F003 [low] documentation** — Parent depth is unchecked when the collection leaf also passes validation

Still present. Parent depth is unchecked only when the collection leaf also passes validation.

**RAV-RUN1-R1-F003 [low] deployment metadata** — Supported logs publish `deployment_type` and `model_availability` as `unknown`

Supported logs normally publish `deployment_type` and `model_availability` as `unknown`, with no CLI override for known facts.

The fix uses validated CLI overrides following the existing platform and engine override pattern.

**RAV-RUN1-R1-F010 [low] test coverage** — The real CLI lacks an end-to-end publication assertion for strict output parsing

The thorough synthetic fixture is useful. An end-to-end publication assertion would also prove strict output parsing through the real CLI.

The existing fixture can drive one CLI publication test that strictly parses and validates each emitted file.
